context.label: Weeks, harvest, and the fiftieth day

observations.body: Israel counts seven complete Sabbaths and fifty days, presents new bread and offerings, holds a holy convocation, and leaves field edges for poor people and foreigners.
observations.label: Seven weeks are counted to a new offering

observations.body: The passage presents Counting fifty days as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Counting fifty days

observations.body: The passage places New meal offering and bread beside Counting fifty days.
observations.label: New meal offering and bread

payload.posture: Read Leviticus 23:15–22 as one movement in Pentecost, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states israel counts seven complete Sabbaths and fifty days, presents new bread and offerings, holds a holy convocation, and leaves field edges for poor people and foreigners. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Pentecost.
payload.title: Seven weeks are counted to a new offering
